newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES CLOSE DOWN 1.9 PCT ON LUJIAZUI.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES CLOSE DOWN 1.9 PCT ON LUJIAZUI.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares fell about 1.9 percent on Tuesday as investors continued to unload shares of property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co, brokers said.
Many investors shied away from entering the market to pick up cheaper shares due to concerns of further falls in Lujiazui, which recently reported poor 1997 interim results, they said.
The B index fell 1.410 points or 1.94 percent to 71.300 on moderate turnover of $6.212 million, compared with $10.067 million on Monday.
"The fall in Lujiazui affected sentiment," said an analyst at a Japanese securities firm. "Lujiazui reported poor results because the Shanghai property market isn't very good."
Lujiazui fell $0.118 or 9.93 percent to $1.070, becoming Tuesday's biggest B share loser.
The company last Friday posted net profits of 179.376 million yuan for the first half of 1997, down 67 percent from the first half of 1996, sparking a sell-off since Monday.
"Looking at the current situation, I think Lujiazui could fall further," the analyst said.

Although the market had expected Lujiazui and other developers with ties to Shanghai's premier Pudong development zone to post weak results, the sharpness of the fall in Lujiazui's interim profit caught some by surprise, analysts said.

Lujiazui and other Pudong plays -- including Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development Co and Shanghai Wai Gaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development Co -- were also looking expensive following sharp gains, they said.
Despite the fall in the B index on Tuesday, market sentiment was sound, which helped to limit losses, brokers said.
Of 47 B shares, 44 shares traded on Tuesday with 27 down, 14 up and three flat.
Recently listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co was the most actively traded B share on profit-taking. It fell $0.020 or 4.37 percent to $0.438 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
Domestic currency A shares tumbled on talk some companies would soon announce poor interim results, causing heavy selling in the afternoon session, brokers said.
The A index fell 39.413 points or 3.18 percent to 1,200.153 on turnover of 3.820 billion yuan from 4.846 billion on Monday.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue chip index plummeted 146.277 points or 3.92 percent to 3,589.552 points.
Both the A and B share markets could fall further on Wednesday due to continued weakness in Lujiazui, brokers said. But the B index should find firm support at around 68 points, they said.
The recent strength of H shares, shares of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong, could also carry over into Shanghai to give the market a boost, some brokers said.
